We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion or religious creed, mental or physical disability, medical condition, genetic information, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, military or veteran status, citizenship, or other characteristics protected by state or federal law or local ordinance.

", "company_logo_url": "https://remotive.com/job/2091134/logo"}, {"id": 2091161, "url": "https://remotive.com/remote-jobs/artificial-intelligence/ai-trainer-video-annotation-2091161", "title": "AI Trainer - Video Annotation", "company_name": "iMerit Technology", "company_logo": "https://remotive.com/job/2091161/logo", "category": "Artificial Intelligence", "tags": ["video", "AI/ML", "robotics"], "job_type": "freelance", "publication_date": "2026-10-22T18:40:19", "candidate_required_location": "Worldwide", "salary": "70K-80K", "description": "

We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

 

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

 

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

 

How it works

 

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
  3. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
  4. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
  5. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
  6. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
  7. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

 

Requirements

 

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering
  • Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
  • Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
  • Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
  • Regular use of an AI coding tool
  • Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
  • You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
  • At least 10 hours a week, starting now

Trade Specialist | U.S. Customs & Client Care

Take your customs expertise beyond the entry.

At GHY, we don’t just move goods across borders. We help businesses navigate complexity, solve problems, and trade with confidence.

For more than a century, we’ve helped importers and exporters navigate global trade. As a Best-Managed Employer and family-led organization, we’ve built our reputation on expertise, integrity, innovation, and genuinely caring about our clients and one another.

If you know customs, enjoy solving problems, and are ready to take greater ownership of the client experience, this could be your next move.

About the Role:

As a Trade Specialist, you’ll go beyond processing customs entries to help ensure our clients receive accurate, consistent, and knowledgeable support.

Reporting to the Client Care Manager, you’ll oversee day-to-day client needs, audit released shipments, maintain client databases and work instructions, and help resolve issues as they arise. You’ll also share your experience with colleagues and support the release team when additional expertise is needed.

This is a great opportunity for an experienced customs professional who is ready to take more ownership, deepen their technical knowledge, and become a trusted resource for both clients and teammates.

What You'll Do:

  • 🤝 Own the client experience. Support day-to-day client needs, answer questions, troubleshoot issues, and help find solutions when challenges arise.🔎
  • Protect quality and accuracy. Audit customs entries and released shipments to identify errors, inconsistencies, and opportunities to improve.
  • 🧠 Be a customs resource. Stay current on CBP regulations and Partner Government Agency requirements, research questions, and help translate regulations into practical guidance.
  • 📞 Keep everyone connected. Communicate professionally with clients, carriers, vendors, Customs, and internal teams to gather information and resolve issues.
  • 📋 Know the client inside and out. Develop and maintain client work instructions, databases, FTA correlations, annual certificates, and other critical account information.
  • 🚚 Step in when it matters. Support accurate customs entry processing across transportation modes when needed to keep shipments moving.
  • 🌱 Share what you know. Assist, coach, and mentor teammates with transactional processing, client requirements, and customs-related questions.
  • 💡 Solve problems before they grow. Recognize risks, use sound judgment, and make timely decisions that help protect both our clients and GHY.

Who You Are:

You know customs, but you also understand that great brokerage service is about more than getting an entry released.

You’re someone who asks questions, catches details others might miss, and takes ownership when something needs to be resolved. You’re equally comfortable digging into regulations, talking with a client, or helping a teammate work through a challenging entry.

You bring:

  • Strong knowledge of U.S. Customs rules and regulations
  • Advanced understanding of customs entry and commercial invoice requirements
  • Working knowledge of Partner Government Agency requirements and entry data elements
  • Knowledge of tariff classification, the General Rules of Interpretation (GRIs), General Notes, and Explanatory Notes
  • Exceptional client service and relationship-building skills
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities
  • Sound judgment when making time-sensitive decisions
  • Experience navigating different client requirements, nuances, and SOPs
  • The ability to prioritize competing demands in a fast-paced environment
  • Clear, positive, and professional written and verbal communication
  • Experience with customs brokerage software
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel
  • The ability to work independently while remaining a collaborative member of the team

What You’ll Bring:

  • 3+ years of customs brokerage or related industry experience
  • Certified Customs Specialist (CCS) designation
  • U.S. Customs Broker License (REQUIRED for Remote Work)
  • Demonstrated experience applying customs knowledge to client needs and transactional processing

Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • ❤️ We CARE: Our values guide how we work: Clients are our focus, Associates matter, Relentlessly serving traders, and Excellence and innovation in all we do.
  • 🏡 Remote Flexibility: Work remotely while staying connected to a collaborative, experienced team.
  • 💰 Competitive Compensation: Fair pay supported by scheduled salary assessments and a performance-based bonus program.
  • 🩺 Excellent Benefits: Comprehensive, subsidized health, dental, vision, short- and long-term disability, and life & AD&D coverage.
  • 📈 Keep Growing: Access ongoing learning through our internal university and leadership development programming.
  • 🤝 More Than Work: Our Giveback Committee, Social Committee, and Cultural Ambassadors create opportunities to connect, contribute, and have some fun along the way.

The Details

📍 Location: We offer flexibility based on experience and location. Candidates within 2 hours of a GHY office may be considered without a U.S. Customs Broker License. For candidates located more than 2 hours from a GHY office, an active U.S. Customs Broker License is required.

🕒 Schedule: Full-time, Monday through Friday, 40 hours per week
📅 Holidays: Two statutory holidays per year may be required

💰 Compensation: Based on experience

Know Customs. Own the Details. Make an Impact.

You’ve built the foundation. Now it’s time to use that experience in a role where your judgment, client service, and customs knowledge make a bigger impact.

At GHY, you’ll solve problems, support clients, share what you know, and continue building your expertise alongside people who understand the complexities of international trade.

Ready to take the next step in your customs career? Apply today.

GHY is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

Salary: $49,000 - $70,000

Why YOU want this position

At Enverus, we're committed to empowering the global quality of life by helping our customers make energy affordable and accessible to the world.

We are the most trusted energy-dedicated SaaS company, with a platform built to maximize value from generative AI, and our innovative solutions are reshaping the way energy is consumed and managed. By offering anytime, anywhere access to analytics and insights, we're helping our customers make better decisions that help provide communities around the world with clean, affordable energy.

The energy industry is changing fast. But we've continued to lead the way in energy technology, creating intelligent connections across the entire energy ecosystem, from renewables, power and utilities, to oil and gas and financial institutions. Our solutions create more efficient production and distribution, capital allocation, renewable energy development, investment and sourcing, and help reduce costs by automating crucial business operations. Of course, this wouldn't be possible without our people, which is why we have built a team of individuals from a diverse range of backgrounds.

Are you ready to help power the global quality of life? Join Enverus, and be a part of creating a brighter, more sustainable tomorrow.

The role

We publish long-term zonal power price forecasts across the North American ISOs. The team builds the view together: the load forecast, the capacity mix and build plan, retirements, fuel, and policy. This seat runs the production cost model that turns that view into hourly hub and zonal prices. How often we can refresh the forecast, and how many questions we can answer with it, depends on this role.

You own the model and help shape the view. You work with the regional analysts on the load, build, and policy assumptions, run the model, validate the output, and explain what it did and why. When the model says something the team did not expect, you are the one who works out whether that is the market or the model.

This is not a client-facing role. You will not be on sales calls or on stage at conferences. You will be in the room when the team forms its view, and your name goes on the research you help shape.

At the Senior Analyst level you run the quarterly cycle without day-to-day supervision. You will have a handover period and Juan to escalate to, but the runs, the diagnostics, and the schedule are yours from the first full cycle.

This role reports to Juan Arteaga, who leads Power Market Fundamentals & Long-Term Forecasting, within the broader Power & Renewables Intelligence group led by Ryan Luther.

This role can be based in any of our North American offices or remote. You will not be in front of clients, but you will be working with our research analysts every single day, so you still need to be someone people want to work with.

A day on the team

Pick up the quarter's updated load forecast from the regional analyst, reconcile it against last quarter, and get it into model-ready shape before the run kicks off.

Launch a full ERCOT run over coffee, then spend the afternoon working out why 2032 summer scarcity hours moved 40% against the last vintage, and which input did it.

Turn around a scenario for an analyst who needs to know what six incremental gigawatts of data center load in PJM does to around-the-clock prices, and have it back to them by Friday.

Work out with the West analyst whether this year's low WECC prices are a durable feature of the renewable build-out or a transitory one, and what the model needs to represent it.

Backcast last year's forecast against what the market actually cleared and work out where the model missed and why.

How we work

Most research shops give ownership of the hardest problems to the most senior person on the team; everyone below executes. We do the opposite. Every analyst, even at entry-level, owns their projects end-to-end and pulls in senior team members for guidance. That hands-on, problem-by-problem ownership is how you build the confidence and judgment to add real value to our clients, and it's the single biggest reason people stay on this team. The modelling is yours in exactly that sense: not a queue of tickets someone else prioritizes for you.

Who thrives in this role

  • You speak well. You can explain what the model did and why, in plain language, to a room that includes people who have never run one, and hold your ground when they push back.
  • You disagree well. When an assumption looks wrong to you, you make the case with evidence and work it through with the team until the view holds up.
  • You're deep where it counts and broad everywhere else. You will know this model better than anyone, and you're just as interested in the market it describes. The best modelers we have worked with can tell you roughly what a result should look like before they hit run.
  • You care more about whether the price is right than how elegant the setup is. You will inherit a model you did not build. The job is to understand it, calibrate it, and improve it, not to replace it with your favourite tool.
  • You ask for help early. You'd rather make ten phone calls and look slightly less smart than struggle alone for two weeks.
  • You understand that excellent and on time outperforms perfect and late.
  • You'd rather write a tight one-pager than a 40-slide deck.
  • You take the work seriously, not yourself.

What you'll own

  • The model. The runs, the inputs, the calibration, and the documentation. When the model produces prices that do not make sense, finding out why is your problem, and when it gets better, that was you.
  • The quarterly cycle. Take the load forecasts and capacity mix build plans the research team produces, integrate them, run the full ISO set, validate the results, and deliver the hub and zonal price files on a published schedule. Every quarter, on time, without a fire drill.
  • Input integration. Turn the team's load, build, retirement, and fuel assumptions into model inputs, on time.
  • Scenario throughput. Run ad hoc scenarios for the research, product, and commercial teams with turnaround measured in days.
  • Validation and diagnostics. Build the checks that catch a bad run before anyone else sees it, and separate the two failure modes cleanly: the model did the wrong thing, which is yours to fix, or the assumption was wrong, which is yours to surface.
  • Explaining the mechanism. When a price view moves between vintages, you are the person who can say which mechanical driver moved it: which units set the margin, which hours, which input changed. Same day.
  • Continuity. Document the model well enough that it survives your vacation, and a different team two years from now.
  • Shaping the view. Work with the regional analysts to build the view: what the assumptions should be and what the model says about them. Co-author the research where your analysis drives the story.

Must-haves

  • 1 to 6 years of hands-on power market modelling, at an IPP, utility, ISO/RTO, consultancy, trading desk, or research/data provider.
  • You communicate clearly and confidently, out loud and in writing. You can walk the team or leadership through why a forecast moved, take hard questions in real time, and leave them understanding the answer.
  • You have been the primary operator of a long-term power price or capacity expansion model in a production setting where other people depended on the output. Consuming someone else's forecast does not count.
  • You bring your own view on supply, demand, and price formation, and you can defend it or change it when the evidence says so.
  • You can calibrate a model to history and tell a real market signal from a model artifact.
  • You understand how a long-term zonal price is actually produced: unit dispatch, marginal units and heat rates, fuel and emissions curves, reserve margins and capacity accreditation, renewable shapes, and how zones trade with each other.
  • Judgment about when a number is wrong, and the instinct to chase it down rather than ship it.
  • You work well with people even though you are not in front of clients. You will take input from half a dozen analysts every cycle, and they need to want to bring you problems.
  • You hit deadlines you did not set. The quarterly cycle has a date on it and clients are waiting on the other side of it.

Helpful, but not required

  • Hands-on experience with a commercial model: Aurora, PLEXOS, EnCompass, GridView, SERVM, Dayzer, or SAInt.
  • Nodal price modelling or power flow experience.
  • Python, SQL, or advanced Excel for handling inputs and outputs.
  • Detailed familiarity with the market design of one or more of ERCOT, PJM, MISO, CAISO, and SPP, or with WECC outside CAISO.
  • Exposure to data center and other large-load forecasting.
  • Graduate work in power systems, operations research, statistics, or economics.

What success looks like in your first 12 months

  • You run your first quarterly cycle with handover support and the next ones on your own, all on schedule.
  • Scenario turnaround is measured in days, and the team stops rationing what it asks the model for.
  • You have backcast the model against recent market outcomes and can show the team where it tracks and where it does not.
  • Someone else on the team can run the model from your runbook. You are not a single point of failure.
  • When research or leadership asks why a price view changed, they get a specific mechanical answer the same day.
  • You have made at least one substantive improvement to the model's mechanics that the research team signs off on.

About Enverus & this team

Enverus is the leading energy SaaS company delivering highly technical insights and predictive/prescriptive analytics that empower customers to make decisions that increase profit. We are a strategic partner to more than 6,000 customers in 50 countries, delivering business-critical insights to the global energy industry through a state-of-the-art SaaS platform built on industry-leading data and analytics.

Our Power & Renewables Intelligence team produces research for institutional investors, hyperscalers, IPP developers, utilities, and corporate strategy teams. If you want to shape how the North American grid gets built over the next decade, this is the place to be.

About Us

At #paid, we’re on a mission to empower creators to do what they love—create. Our marketplace connects vetted creators with some of the world’s most iconic brands, like McDonald’s, Samsung, and Disney, fostering authentic collaborations that drive real business results. We’ve built a marketplace that solves big challenges in the creator ecosystem, from fair pricing to algorithmic matching and content usage rights, ensuring every partnership is seamless and impactful.
With our proprietary technology and an unwavering commitment to trust and transparency, we’re revolutionizing the way brands and creators come together to make magic. Rated #1 for customer support and managed services, #paid is leading the creator marketing space. Through innovative technology and a team of ambitious humans, we're transforming the future of the creator economy.

The Role

Creative Solutions now owns execution from end to end, so strategy has to cover the whole span: pre-sale (discovery, ideation, proposals) and post-sale (kickoff strategy, campaign briefs, post-campaign insights). As a Strategist on this team, you’ll shape the idea that wins the pitch and stay with it until it ships, performs, and turns into a renewal. Our goal is simple: the idea that wins the pitch is the idea that ships.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the core insight and creative idea, plus the integrated plan behind it: creators, media and distribution, and measurement
  • Build proposals and RFP responses with a clear, data-backed case for #paid
  • Set the creator mix: when to scale with micro and niche creators, when to concentrate on macro names, and how to combine both
  • Build the investment plan, splitting budget across organic content, usage rights and paid amplification, and set channel mix and flighting
  • Define KPIs and benchmarks up front, optimize in flight, and turn results into renewal stories
  • Stay involved post-sale with creator briefs, content direction, and strategic QA
  • Stay ahead of market and platform changes, and translate them into sharper proposal work
  • Contribute to proactive packages and first-to-market moments
  • This person covers the whole creator-campaign lifecycle, from pre-sale ideation through post-campaign insights, with a stronger emphasis on creator mix, budget planning, and measurement

To Be Successful, You'll Need

  • Deliver integrated ideas that ship and perform
  • Use data to sharpen an idea rather than decorate it
  • Plan and defend budget allocations across paid social
  • Design measurement plans and act on performance data
  • Communicate strategy clearly in writing and in client presentations
  • Design and build decks with strong visual and narrative craft
  • Use AI tools to inform research and accelerate the creative process
  • Manage several projects at once under tight deadlines
  • Own ambiguous, high-stakes proposals independently, and drive decisions across functions without formal authority

About You

  • 5+ years in strategy, creative, social, or creator marketing (or equivalent demonstrated experience), ideally on the agency or platform side
  • Strong deck craft and real fluency in the same five platforms

About the company

At Nuitée, we are building the API backbone for the global travel industry. Founded in 2017, Nuitée is on a mission to transform a fragmented travel ecosystem with simple, scalable, and API-first infrastructure—think “Stripe for Travel.”

By enabling seamless connectivity between hotels, OTAs, fintechs, super-apps, and businesses, some of which are entering the travel market for the first time, Nuitée empowers companies to deliver reliable travel products effortlessly. Our robust platform simplifies complex supplier networks, offering direct access to hotel inventory with better pricing, coverage, and technology.

With teams across the globe, including hubs in London, New York, San Francisco, Palma de Mallorca and Casablanca, Nuitée has grown into a global infrastructure provider trusted by industry leaders like Hopper, Priceline, Google, and Uber.

Now backed by leading VCs and world-class investors including leaders from , Stripe, and Shopify, Nuitée is positioned to redefine the B2B travel market, streamline operations for hotels, and enable new applications through cutting-edge APIs.

Nuitée is at the forefront of a revolution—delivering AI-powered, smarter, and more personalized travel experiences for a new era.

About the role

Remote in Europe, or hybrid in Barcelona, Dublin, London, or Palma.

Want to help build a new kind of engineering team?

At Nuitée, you'll work across a complex travel marketplace, from pricing and inventory to hotel mapping and booking systems. You'll identify what's limiting performance, decide what needs improving, ship the changes yourself, and see the impact on bookings, market share, and margin.

As one of the first engineers in our new Field Engineering team, you'll work closely with Account Management to tackle the technical challenges behind the growth of our largest enterprise accounts. That might mean optimising pricing to win more hotel bookings without sacrificing margin, improving availability across thousands of properties, or building better recovery mechanisms for failed bookings.

You'll follow problems across the platform rather than staying within one service. When something works, you'll help turn it into a reusable capability across Nuitée.

You'll build on an approach that's already delivered results for a major partner, bring it to more accounts, and help shape the function from its early days.

What makes it interesting for you

  • You can ship while it matters. Account-specific changes can go live the same day, and you can immediately track whether the numbers move.

  • You get the full picture. AMs bring customer context and market-share data; you decide which engineering changes can make the biggest difference.

  • You'll shape how Field Engineering scales. As an early hire, you'll help develop the playbook, share fixes, and turn repeatable solutions into product capabilities.

Your offer comes with meaningful equity. Nuitée has grown 10x since 2022, was profitable before raising a $48M Series A led by Accel, and works with companies such as Revolut, Grab, Hopper, Priceline, and Sabre.

The kind of problems you'll work on

  • Why are we losing bookings to competing suppliers, and what changes to pricing, availability, or mapping would win more without sacrificing margin?

  • How do we keep a hotel rate shown in search available at that price when the customer books?

  • How can better prebook and booking recovery mechanisms increase successful transactions?

  • Which solutions developed for one account should become reusable capabilities across the platform?

This role fits if you

  • Are a deeply hands-on, Staff-level software engineer with a track record of building complex production systems.

  • Can trace problems across backend services, APIs, data flows, and external dependencies, then implement solutions yourself.

  • Understand how technical decisions affect customers, product performance, and commercial outcomes.

  • Have taken ambiguous engineering problems from diagnosis through production and measured the impact.

  • Explain complex technical topics clearly and work well with Product and commercial teams.

Experience with marketplaces, pricing, transactional platforms, or complex API products is particularly relevant. Go experience is a plus, but not required for experienced engineers. Travel industry experience isn't necessary either.

Nuitée moves quickly, has little process, and gives people a lot of room to make decisions. You’ll do well here if ambiguity does not slow you down, you like going deep into difficult problems, and you want to be accountable for what your work actually delivers.

If this sounds interesting, we’d love to hear from you. You can apply with your LinkedIn profile or CV. The process is straightforward and typically takes ~3 weeks.

Why Nuitee?

At Nuitée, we’re not just reimagining travel—we’re building the infrastructure to power it.

  • Massive Market Opportunity: We are tackling the $9.9tn travel industry, starting with the $75 billion B2B hotel market, a fragmented space filled with outdated systems, gatekeepers, and inefficiencies. Nuitée’s API-first platform is solving this, enabling businesses to access hotel inventory seamlessly and at scale.
  • World-Class Backing: Backed by Accel and visionary leaders across tech and travel—including Booking.com, Stripe, and Shopify—we’re equipped to scale our ambition globally.
  • Bootstrapped Resilience, Startup Agility: Having grown profitably for years without external funding, we combine operational discipline with the speed and innovation of a scaling startup.
  • Global Impact: Our infrastructure supports partners like Google, Grab, worldwide fintechs, superapps, travel companies and others
  • AI-Driven Innovation: Nuitée is uniquely positioned to power the future of travel in the AI era—enabling seamless, intelligent, and hyper-personalized travel interactions.

By joining Nuitée, you’ll be part of a team that’s building a category-defining platform. You’ll work on a global scale, innovate alongside industry leaders, and help drive the next phase of travel technology. If you’re excited to push boundaries, redefine a multi-trillion-dollar industry, and grow with us—Nuitée is the place for you.

By submitting your application, you consent to Nuitée processing your personal data for the purposes of assessing your suitability for employment. Your information will be stored securely and will only be retained for as long as necessary for the recruitment process, or up to 6 months afterward, in accordance with our data protection policy and applicable laws. You have the right to request access, correction, or deletion of your personal data at any time by contacting us at . For more details, please see our Privacy Policy: Nuitée Privacy Notice 2026.

AECOM’s Technology Solutions Group (TSG) is seeking an exceptional mid-level Information & Communication Technologies (ICT) Consultant to join our ICT Data Center Team. The successful candidate will bring strong communication, follow-through, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. This is a remote position open to candidates across the United States, with a hybrid option available for those near an AECOM office.

The Information & Communication Technologies (ICT) Consultant will have or develop a solid understanding of Data Center client business practices and goals to:

  • Work on a team of ICT designers and BIM specialists to produce quality constructable data center design documents on schedule.
  • Develop and formulate solutions to Data Center client problems on assigned projects
  • Have broad technical knowledge but possesses an area of specialization or focus
  • Apply in-depth knowledge of Data Center ICT Infrastructure types and uses to perform complex and unique assignments including survey, design, development, and construction administration of Data Center ICT infrastructure projects.
  • Be responsible for ICT design and consulting for:
    • Hyper-Scale Data Centers
    • Enterprise Data Centers
    • Structured Cabling Systems (SCS)
    • Campus / Wide Area Networks (WAN)
    • Passive Optical Networks (PON)
    • Outside Plant (OSP)
  • Perform specific and/or limited ICT Design and Consulting duties as part of a larger Data Center Design team of expert Consultants.
  • Gather and correlate engineering data using established and well-defined procedures.
  • Work on detailed and/or routine design and/or consulting assignments.
  • Propose solutions to solve new and/or complex problems encountered.
  • Provide guidance and direction to internal mid-level consultants and production staff.
  • Perform work in accordance with the agreed-upon budget and schedule with minimal supervision

AECOM’s Buildings + Places practice includes architecture, interiors, building engineering, workplace strategy, business transformation, asset advisory, economics and development planning, master planning, urban planning, and landscape architecture. With a range of expertise from strategy and design through project realization, we create better outcomes to grow economies, protect natural systems, conserve natural resources, make societies more equitable, and connect and engage people through innovative, sustainable design solutions. Our teams have worked on signature projects such as the London 2012 Olympic Park and Legacy Framework, to the new plan for the LA2028 Olympics, to industrial facilities for GE and Rolls-Royce, to headquarters and workplaces for NASA, Unilever, Sony Music, DirecTV, Box, Inc., and many Fortune 500 companies.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college/university plus six (6) years of relevant experience, or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
  • Data Center design experience with ICT infrastructure
  • Current BICSI Registered Communications Distribution Designer (RCDD) Certification
  • Due to the nature of the work, U.S. Citizenship or lawful permanent residency (Green Card) is required

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3 years’ Hyper-Scale Data Center design experience with ICT infrastructure
  • Professional experience and/or proficiency in various software products, including but not limited to, Revit, AutoCAD, Visio Professional, Bluebeam Extreme (Revu), Microsoft Project, Microsoft 365 Suite (Word, Excel, Power Point, etc.) and other ICT Specific Programs
  • Professional experience and/or proficiency in various Codes Standards and regulations including but not limited to Permitting, State & Local Ordinances, IEEE – C2 Standard (National Electrical Safety Code), OSHA - 1910 Standards, TIA – Cabling Standards, TIA – Data Center Standards and BICSI – TDMM and other Manuals
  • Other active BICSI Certifications (BICSI DCDC certification is a plus)

Additional Information:

  • Relocation is not available for this position
  • Sponsorship is not available for this position
  • THIS POSTING IS FOR A CURRENT VACANCY, AND AECOM INTENDS TO FILL THIS POSITION BY Feb 1, 2027

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Root was founded on the belief that car insurance is broken, and we set out to change it. We’re harnessing the power of technology to revolutionize this archaic, complicated industry. Using machine learning and mobile telematic platforms, we’ve built one of the most innovative insurtech companies in the world.

The Opportunity

We believe that a disruptive insurance company must have a principled quantitative framework at its foundation. At Root, we are committed to the rigorous development and effective deployment of modern statistical machine learning methods to problems in the insurance industry.

As a Lead Actuary I, you will own complex pricing work from problem definition through implementation. In this role, you will lead the development of tools and frameworks to file and deploy auto pricing and product updates more efficiently. You will work cross-functionally with State Product Management and Engineering, and regularly engage with Root’s executive team to align technical insights with strategic priorities.

At Root, we are building a more efficient, data-driven approach to insurance pricing. Our Actuarial Pricing team supports regulatory filings, develops rate indications, evaluates pricing performance, and partners across the organization to help Root make well-informed decisions about risk, growth, and profitability. To advance this work, we are looking for a Lead Actuary I who can improve and automate existing processes, utilizing AI technologies where appropriate while maintaining rigor and regulatory compliance.

Salary Range: $107,800 - $134,700(Eligible for competitive bonus and equity offering)

Root is a “work where it works best” company. Meaning we will support you working in whatever location that works best for you across the US. We will continue to have our headquarters in Columbus, Ohio.

How You Will Make an Impact

  • Prepare, review, and support end-to-end rate filings, including actuarial exhibits, supporting documentation, implementation requirements, and responses to regulatory objections.
  • Own complex actuarial pricing projects, including rate level indications, pricing analyses, state expansion work, refunds, and other initiatives that support Root’s growth and profitability.
  • Serve as a filing manager or technical reviewer for filings prepared by other actuaries, providing clear feedback and ensuring that work is accurate, complete, well-supported, and ready for submission.
  • Develop and communicate actuarial recommendations by evaluating data, methodologies, assumptions, business context, and regulatory considerations.
  • Act as a subject-matter expert in one or more areas of actuarial pricing, such as rate level indications, state-specific pricing, rate level analysis, refunds, predictive-model implementation, or filing operations.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the filing process and pricing workflow through better documentation, reusable frameworks, automation, and effective use of data and technology, including GenAI.
  • Partner with Product, State Management, Regulatory, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, and other teams to translate technical analysis into clear business decisions.
  • Proactively identify risks, dependencies, and missing information that could affect filing, launch, or implementation timelines.
  • Communicate complex actuarial concepts and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior leaders.
  • Coach and support other actuaries through technical collaboration, review, knowledge sharing, and development of team standards.
  • Balance independent execution with effective prioritization, escalating decisions and risks when appropriate while maintaining forward momentum.

What You Will Need to Succeed

  • 5+ years of experience in the insurance industry, including 3+ years of experience in actuarial pricing, ratemaking, or a related discipline.
  • Experience with personal lines property and casualty insurance, preferably auto insurance.
  • Experience developing or reviewing rate level indications and supporting regulatory rate filings.
  • Experience building actuarial automation, filing tools, or scalable pricing processes.
  • Independently frames complex problems, evaluates options, and communicates clear recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong actuarial judgment and the ability to evaluate methodologies, assumptions, data limitations, and business tradeoffs.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently frame problems, assess options, recommend a path forward, and deliver results across multiple workstreams.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical topics clearly and concisely.
  • Experience with SQL, R, Python, or similar analytical tools.
  • Demonstrated ownership mentality, including proactively identifying opportunities, risks, and process improvements.
  • Ability to work effectively in a highly collaborative, cross-functional environment.
  • Successful completion of at least five actuarial exams.
  • Preferred but not required:
    • ACAS designation.
    • Experience with more complex regulatory jurisdictions.
    • Experience with predictive modeling, machine learning, or model implementation.
    • Experience with Git, cloud computing, or production-oriented analytical workflows.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Account Executive to join our Pharmacy Benefit Management (PBM) team. The successful candidate will be responsible for managing key client relationships, taking a consultative approach to account management, ensuring the delivery of high-quality pharmacy benefits, and driving client satisfaction. This role requires a deep understanding of PBM services, strong communication skills, and the ability to manage complex accounts.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Responsible for the overall relationship with assigned PBM clients, including managing ongoing client touchbases, contract deliverables, tracking client inquiries and maintaining logs, resolving client escalations when they occur, and ensuring overall client satisfaction.
  • Maintain regular contact with clients, client representatives, and other internal members of the account team regarding ongoing pharmacy operations.
  • Serve as the initial point of contact for all day-to-day operational inquiries, either from clients directly or from internal team members on behalf of the client. Lead and facilitate all client meetings, including quarterly and annual business reviews.
  • Partner with the Implementation Team during new client implementations to ensure a seamless transition from implementation to client management post-launch.
  • Responsible for gathering all client requirements for the annual open enrollment process, including benefit changes and any customized requirements.
  • Participate in client webinars, training, and other forums designed to educate their employees on Righway’s PBM solution. Travel to client sites for Open Enrollment or Benefit Fairs may be required.
  • Identify trends within issues and work with the operations team and vendor partners to take appropriate preventative measures.
  • Work with operations and vendor partners to ensure all requirements and deliverables are met and sent to the client timely and accurately. Ability to track and identify issues and risks that are not being met per contractual obligations.
  • Participate in efforts to support standardization across accounts and work in multi-disciplinary teams to design and implement production and operational enhancements.
  • Provide ongoing support to Rightway partners which may include, but is not limited to, interpreting plan design, researching and resolving phone, written and electronic inquiries, and resolving claims, benefit and enrollment issues.
  • Maintain an understanding of industry trends and provide clients with insights and recommendations on how Rightway’s solutions work to address those trends.

WHO YOU ARE:

  • Education level: Bachelor’s Degree Required. Preferred: Master’s Degree
  • Work experience: 5-8 years in pharmacy operations
  • Location information: Remote or Dallas, TX
  • Important characteristics of ideal candidate: Detail-oriented, consultative and presentation skills, excellent communication & organization skills, ability to bring stakeholders together to identify solutions to challenges
  • Specific skills needed for the job: Solid client management skills, pharmacy benefit knowledge, effective & creative problem-solving, ability to prioritize and manage through change. Solid communication skills, ability to lead projects and influence others even without direct reporting line ownership. Basic knowledge of common spreadsheet tools (Excel, Google Sheets) and Presentation Tools (Power Point, Google Slides)

COMPENSATION: $125,000 - $145,000 annually, in addition to bonus and equity

Compensation offered will be determined by geographic location, experience, and qualifications.

CYBERSECURITY AWARENESS NOTICE

In response to ongoing and industry-wide fraudulent recruitment activities (i.e., job scams), Rightway wants to inform potential candidates that we will only contact them from the @ email domain. We will never ask for bank details or deposits of any kind as a condition of employment.

ABOUT RIGHTWAY:

Rightway is on a mission to harmonize healthcare for everyone, everywhere. Our products guide patients to the best care and medications by inserting clinicians and pharmacists into a patient’s care journey through a modern, mobile app. Rightway is a front door to healthcare, giving patients the tools they need along with on-demand access to Rightway health guides, human experts that answer their questions and manage the frustrating parts of healthcare for them.

Since its founding in 2017, Rightway has raised over $300mm from investors including Khosla Ventures, Thrive Capital, Francisco Partners, and Tiger Global. We’re headquartered in New York City, with satellite offices in Denver and Dallas. Our clients rely on us to transform the healthcare experience, improve outcomes for their teams, and decrease their healthcare costs.

HOW WE LIVE OUR VALUES TO OUR TEAMMATES:

We’re seeking those with passion for healthcare and relentless devotion to our goal. We need team members that embody our core values:

1) We are human, firstOur humanity binds us together. We bring the same empathetic approach to every individual we engage with, whether it be our members, our clients, or each other. We are all worthy of respect and understanding and we engage in our interactions with care and intention. We honor our stories. We listen to—and hear—each other, we celebrate our differences and similarities, we are present for each other, and we strive for mutual understanding.

2) We redefine what is possibleWe always look beyond the obstacles in front of us to imagine new solutions. We approach our work with inspiration from other industries, other leaders, and other challenges. We use ingenuity and resourcefulness when faced with tough problems.

3) We debate then commitWe believe that a spirit of open discourse is part of a healthy culture. We understand and appreciate different perspectives and we challenge our assumptions. When working toward a decision or a new solution, we actively listen to one another, approach it with a “yes, and” mentality, and assume positive intent. Once a decision is made, we align and champion it as one team.

4) We cultivate gritChanging healthcare doesn’t happen overnight. We reflect and learn from challenges and approach the future with a determination to strive for better. In the face of daunting situations, we value persistence. We embrace failure as a stepping stone to future success. On this journey, we seek to act with guts, resilience, initiative, and tenacity.

5) We seek to delightHealthcare is complicated and personal. We work tirelessly to meet the goals of our clients while also delivering the best experience to our members. We recognize that no matter the role or team, we each play a crucial part in our members’ care and take that responsibility seriously. When faced with an obstacle, we are kind, respectful, and solution-oriented in our approach. We hold ourselves accountable to our clients and our members’ success.

Rightway is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer that believes in the strength of diverse thought, beliefs, backgrounds, and education. We foster an inclusive culture where differences are celebrated to drive the best business decisions possible. We do not discriminate on any basis protected by applicable law. All employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, need, and performance.

      <media:content url="https://wwr-pro.s3.amazonaws.com/logos/0171/3386/logo.gif" type="image/png"/>
      <title>Sanctuary Computer: Head of Technology</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description><img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0171/3386/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" />

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> New York City
    <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://sanctuary.computer">https://sanctuary.computer</a>
</p>

<p>We are hiring a <strong>Head of Technology</strong> for the garden3d creative collective, to lead engineering at Sanctuary Computer and garden3d in the era of agentic computer code.</p>
<p><a href="https://garden3d.notion.site/Head-of-Technology-3f9131fea2c7815da5e3ec914835c397?source=copy_link"><strong>Original job posting link</strong></a></p>
<h3><strong>About <a href="https://garden3d.net/">garden3d</a></strong></h3>
<p>We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.</p>
<p>Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy &amp; Gagosian.</p>
<p>We’re the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone &amp; Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.</p>
<p>We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.</p>
<h3><strong>Sanctuary Computer - Development</strong></h3>
<p>At <strong><a href="https://www.sanctuary.computer/">Sanctuary Computer</a></strong> we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.</p>
<p>Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.</p>
<h3><strong>XXIX - Design</strong></h3>
<p>When we started <strong><a href="https://www.xxix.co/">XXIX</a></strong> in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.</p>
<p>We’re building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.</p>
<h3><strong>Index - Community</strong></h3>
<p><strong><a href="https://www.index-space.org/">Index</a></strong> is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.</p>
<p>We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.</p>
<h3><strong><a href="https://feed.garden3d.net/">garden3d TK</a> — Media</strong></h3>
<p>At garden3d, we’re in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.</p>
<p>We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.</p>
<p>Plus, our partner organizations</p>
<p><strong><a href="https://www.thelightphone.com/">Lightphone</a><br></strong><strong><a href="https://www.mill.com/">Mill</a><br></strong><strong><a href="https://ingredient-ai.com/">IngredientAI</a></strong></p>
<h2>⛰️ The Head of Technology Role</h2>
<p>The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder &amp; president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.</p>
<p>You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.</p>
<p>This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.</p>
<p>This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.</p>
<p>They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.</p>
<p>They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&amp;L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world.</p>
<h2><strong>Responsibilities &amp; Mandates</strong></h2>
<h3>️ <strong>Systems that hold up</strong></h3>
<p>We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out.</p>
<h3> <strong>All in on agentic development</strong></h3>
<p>The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.</p>
<h3> <strong>Practical engineering</strong></h3>
<p>We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value engineering: the simplest thing that works, built well, at a cost the client is glad to pay.</p>
<h3> <strong>Code quality at Sanctuary Computer</strong></h3>
<p>Sanctuary Computer is where our engineering standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They set what good code review looks like, keep our senior developers sharp on architecture and quality, and make sure that bar holds without slowing the team down.</p>
<h3> <strong>Hiring and empowering the very best</strong></h3>
<p>They are a magnet for exceptional engineers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so.</p>
<h3> <strong>Estimation, scoping and delivery</strong></h3>
<p>They make sure our teams can reliably estimate and story point the work ahead, and that we deliver at a pace that meets the dates we promised and protects our margins. When an estimate is wrong, they find out why and fix the process.</p>
<h3> <strong>The technical voice in new business</strong></h3>
<p>Our clients include Google, Stripe, Figma, Mozilla and The Nobel Prize. This person joins new business calls as the trusted technical consultant, scopes the work, writes the technical side of proposals, and can explain a hard tradeoff to a client's CTO and their CEO in the same meeting.</p>
<h3> <strong>Hardware sense</strong></h3>
<p>We're the software team behind The Light Phone and Mill, so a good share of our work touches devices. This person doesn't need to be a firmware engineer, but they understand how hardware works, where it constrains the software, and how to plan a project that spans both.</p>
<h3> <strong>The garden3d technology story</strong></h3>
<p>Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.</p>
<h3> <strong>Culture</strong></h3>
<p>They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The engineers they lead do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is earned, and the craft rubs off</p>
<h3>&nbsp;<strong>Special Projects</strong></h3>
<p>In addition to day to day responsibilities, here’s an idea of some of the projects this role may spearhead or support in coming years →</p>
<ul>
<li>Making agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer builds, with loops and evals the whole team trusts</li>
<li>Setting the shared technical conventions every garden3d studio builds from</li>
<li>Landing the kind of flagship engineering engagement that changes what people think we do</li>
<li>Hiring the next generation of the engineering team, across every garden3d studio</li>
<li>Turning the internal tools and agents we build for ourselves into products</li>
<li>Partnering with the Head of Design so our own studio websites are as well engineered as they are designed</li>
</ul>
<h2>Qualifications</h2>
<p>This is a great opportunity for someone looking to make a significant impact in a growing, dynamic company. Based on the responsibilities of this role, we think the right candidate has the following experience and skills:</p>
<p><strong> Must have:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>12+ years building software, at least three of them leading engineers inside a studio, agency, startup or founder-led company</li>
<li>Deep experience engineering complex systems, shipped and run in production: distributed services, data pipelines, multi-platform products</li>
<li>A true technology generalist, comfortable across frontend, backend, data, infrastructure and native</li>
<li>A strong preference for practical engineering: convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms as a service over bespoke infrastructure</li>
<li>All in on agentic development: loop engineering, evals, and agents doing real work in a real codebase</li>
<li>Fluency across most of our stack: React, Next.js, Ruby on Rails, Elixir &amp; Phoenix, Sanity, Postgres, Redis. You won't use all of it every week, but you should be able to review any of it</li>
<li>Experience as the technical lead in winning work: scoping, estimating and pitching to clients</li>
<li>A track record of hiring exceptional engineers, and of people who got measurably better working for them</li>
<li>Hands-on. This person can still write the code, not only review it (and will get on the tools when the need arises)</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Nice-to-have:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>A sense of how hardware works: firmware, embedded systems, IoT, and shipping software for physical products</li>
<li>Experience in a client services environment (a consultancy, agency or studio)</li>
<li>Experience in a Sales Engineer or Solutions Architect role</li>
<li>Open source projects they've started or maintained</li>
<li>Experience fostering close collaboration between design and engineering teams</li>
<li>Experience inside a worker-owned, open-book, or otherwise unusual company</li>
<li>A network in the engineering community: the meetups, the conferences, the people worth hiring</li>
<li>Interests in design, art, music, food or fashion. We find these people have a well rounded sense of quality</li>
</ul>
<h2> Who you are</h2>
<p>The person we’re looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with and appreciates a commitment to a culture of transparency, non-dictatorial leadership styles, and alternative methodologies. They’re flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work “smart” by carefully managing their workflow and team.</p>
<h2> How we interview</h2>
<p>After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.</p>
<p>From there, we’ll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where we’re going as a business.</p>
<p>For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.</p>
<h2> Compensation</h2>
<p><strong>This is a permanent leadership role.</strong> If this individual exceeds expectations in their first four months, we'll shape the permanent role together, with scope and compensation that grow as the studios and their revenue do. After a period of proven success (12 - 24 months), they become eligible to join our worker ownership program.</p>
<p>We start with a 4-month fraction trial contract, paid hourly between <strong>$110 - $175</strong> p/hr pending seniority &amp; experience. In the first few weeks of the trial, this individual will propose their own goals to define success in their trial, and present them to our leadership team for approval.</p>
<p>At garden3d, we believe that those who shoulder the most responsibility and create the greatest impact should be paid accordingly. This role greatly favors autonomous, competent &amp; ambitious operators.</p>
<h2>‍ <strong>How we work:</strong></h2>
<p>We believe that there’s a better balance between the poles of freelancing &amp; full time, and for that reason we work differently to most shops:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong><a href="https://sanctucompu.substack.com/p/our-open-source-2020-profit-and-loss">Transparency &amp; Ownership</a>:</strong>&nbsp;We release out Profit &amp; Loss statements to the community each year, open source our best ideas, and talk business &amp; money with everyone in the company. We’re proud to run our business with integrity, and for that reason we share everything with our team &amp; community.</li>
<li><strong><a href="https://negative.sanctuary.computer/">150% Carbon Negative</a>:</strong> Our studio offsets 150% of the carbon we use to do business each year, dated back to our founding in 2015. We turn down work that is not in-line with our morals, and we encourage our peers to do the same. <a href="https://twitter.com/sanctucompu/status/1385282161197060100">We have been certified climate neutral since 2021</a>.</li>
<li><strong><a href="https://sanctucompu.substack.com/p/our-moral-compass">Strong Morals</a>:</strong> Since our founding, we've turned down somewhere between $1mm - $2mm of work that didn't meet our moral standards. (Most of that was DTC brands that can't show a valid sustainability initiative).</li>
<li><strong>Async &amp; Decentralized:</strong> We use tools optimized for calm, thoughtful communication, and opt for async whenever possible. We fight hard to maintain our focus time.</li>
<li><strong>Remote Friendly:</strong>&nbsp;Our company is fluent in remote work, making our workplace more decentralized, and democratized in the process.</li>
<li><strong>Ideas &amp; Products:</strong>&nbsp;In our spare studio time, we work to build our own open source or internal products to diversify &amp; bolster our income. We create amazing technology products for our clients, so why not for the studio?</li>
</ul>
<p>→ Read more on our <a href="https://sanctucompu.substack.com/">Substack, over here</a>.</p>
<h2><strong> How to apply</strong></h2>
<p>We’re excited to hear from you! ❤</p>
<p><strong>Kindly submit a complete and thoughtful application, including relevant links that help verify your work experience and identity. Applications with missing or insufficient information will not move forward in the review process.</strong></p>
<p><strong>Our team carefully reviews every complete submission, and we truly appreciate the time and effort you put into applying! :)</strong></p>

<p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/sanctuary-computer-head-of-technology">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/sanctuary-computer-head-of-technology</a></p>
</description>

      <title>Samsara: Staff Software Engineer</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote
    <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://www.samsara.com/">https://www.samsara.com/</a>
</p>

<p><strong>About the role:</strong></p>
<p>Samsara (NYSE: IOT) sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world. The platform processes 25+ trillion data points annually from IoT sensors, cameras, and connected devices across thousands of organizations, and that dataset is compounding: it grew from 4 trillion to 25+ trillion in four years. We're still early in turning that data into the products that will define how physical operations run, and we're hiring the engineers who will build what comes next.</p>
<p>We're approaching ~$2B ARR growing 30%+ year over year, with 96% of our largest customers on two or more products. The fastest-growing divisions at Samsara are tackling the hardest, most ambiguous problems at the company: building new products from scratch, applying AI and ML to massive real-world datasets, and shipping capabilities that change how organizations maintain equipment, manage fleets, and run day-to-day operations. Most of this work is zero-to-one, at billion-dollar scale.</p>
<p>We're looking for software engineers who want to define what ships next. Leveling is broad and flexible: we're hiring from Senior through Staff+, across platform and product, and we're open to shaping scope around the right person's strengths and interests. That window won't stay open long.</p>
<p><strong>This role is remote and open to candidates residing in the US. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.</strong></p>
<p><strong>You should apply if:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>You want to impact the industries that run our world.</strong>&nbsp;The software you build will have real-world stakes: helping keep the lights on, getting food into grocery stores, keeping workers safe. What ships here isn't metrics on a dashboard. It shows up on the loading dock, the job site, and the dispatch floor.</li>
<li><strong>You want to build, not maintain.</strong>&nbsp;Samsara is in full growth mode. We're building new systems from scratch, not babysitting old ones. You'd own entire problem spaces end to end, with the autonomy to set direction from day one.</li>
<li><strong>You want to work where AI meets the physical world.</strong>&nbsp;Samsara has spent a decade building the largest proprietary dataset for physical operations. More connected assets generate more data, more data trains better models, better models drive more value, and more value wins more assets. The market and the opportunity here are what set us apart, not just the models.</li>
<li><strong>You believe customers are more than a number.</strong>&nbsp;Samsara engineers have a rare closeness to end users. You'll participate in customer interviews, collaborate with product managers and customer success, and use that context to build products that solve real problems operators face every day.</li>
<li><strong>You have the curiosity and drive to figure it out.</strong>&nbsp;We're looking for people who take pride in their work and get things done at all costs. The engineers who thrive here don't wait to be told what to build. They define it, ship it, and own the outcome. The rate-limiting step on our teams isn't tooling or process. It's ambition.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>In this role, you will:</strong>&nbsp;</p>
<ul>
<li>Take ownership of technically complex, mission-critical areas and run with them. We want to point you in a direction and show up to the demo meeting impressed, not spend our weeks managing the details.</li>
<li>Define and drive technical strategy for new products and platform capabilities, from backend services and APIs to the customer-facing UI.</li>
<li>Design and ship full-stack features end to end. You'll work across backend, frontend, and potentially mobile to deliver AI-powered products that solve real operational problems.</li>
<li>Partner with product, design, and customer-facing teams to translate ambiguous, real-world problems into clear technical plans and measurable outcomes.</li>
<li>Build and scale the systems behind AI-driven products, including data ingestion, APIs, and the workflows that put intelligence into the hands of operators.</li>
<li>Raise the bar for the engineers around you through code reviews, design reviews, technical mentorship, and by setting a standard for quality, velocity, and craft.</li>
<li>Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Minimum requirements for the role:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.</li>
<li>8+ years of experience in software design and development, including building and operating production systems at scale.</li>
<li>Strong full-stack fundamentals. You're comfortable working across backend services, APIs, and frontend (web or mobile) to ship complete products.</li>
<li>Proficiency in modern languages and frameworks (Go, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, React, or similar).</li>
<li>Demonstrated experience leading cross-team or cross-org projects from inception through rollout, including managing ambiguity, driving alignment, and delivering measurable impact.</li>
<li>Experience building AI-powered or data-driven products. You don't need to train models, but you know how to take AI capabilities and turn them into products customers love.</li>
<li>Strong communication skills and the ability to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders.</li>
<li>A track record of building: zero-to-one products, systems you left in a meaningfully better place, or hard problems you refused to let stay unsolved.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>An ideal candidate also has:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Experience shipping AI-powered features in production, whether that's LLM-based products, agentic workflows, recommendation systems, or other customer-facing AI.</li>
<li>Comfort with modern AI-augmented development workflows (Cursor, LLMs, etc.) to multiply your output and accelerate delivery.</li>
<li>Background working with real-world operational data (telematics, sensor data, work orders, inspections) or a strong interest in learning the domain.</li>
<li>A proven track record of mentoring senior engineers and influencing engineering culture, standards, and best practices beyond a single team.</li>
<li>Side projects, open-source contributions, or other signals of curiosity and drive outside the scope of your day job.</li>
</ul>
<div class="content-pay-transparency">
<div class="pay-input">
<div class="description">
<p>The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.</p>
</div>
<div class="title">Annual Base Salary</div>
<div class="pay-range">$162,400<span class="divider">—</span>$290,000 USD</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="content-conclusion">
<p><strong>Total Rewards</strong></p>
<p>At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why&nbsp;<a href="https://www.samsara.com/company/careers/benefits">our rewards</a>&nbsp;are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.</p>
<p>Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.</p>
<p><strong>Flexible Working&nbsp;</strong></p>
<p>At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.</p>
<p><strong>Belonging at Samsara</strong></p>
<p>At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.</p>
</div>

<p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/samsara-staff-software-engineer">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/samsara-staff-software-engineer</a></p>
</description>
